lead.event: IDX plans HSC-stock exclusion and shareholder-transparency reforms
lead.headline: IDX plans to exclude 80 HSC stocks from IHSG calculation
lead.blurb: The 80 High Shareholding Concentration stocks will remain listed and tradable, but their price movements will no longer affect the IHSG. They account for about 18% of its weight, which BEI plans to redistribute to more liquid stocks with adequate free float while adjusting the divisor to avoid mechanical moves. The change is due at the start of November, and BEI will also label ownership data for shareholders holding 1% or more as affiliate or non-affiliate.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Bank Mandiri and BNI strengthen capital through AT1 issuances
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BMRI and BBNI strengthen capital with US$1.45 billion in AT1 issues
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Bank Mandiri issued a US$750 million perpetual bond in late September, while BNI completed a US$700 million AT1 issuance in April at a 7.15% annual yield. Both were counted as additional core capital, and BNI plans to repurchase most of its 2021 AT1 instruments.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: ADRO and AADI begin shareholder-approved share buybacks
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: ADRO and AADI begin shareholder-approved buybacks capped at Rp10 trillion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Alamtri Resources and Adaro Andalan Indonesia each have a Rp5 trillion ceiling. ADRO’s program runs through April 2027, while AADI’s runs until 22 May 2027.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Indonesian issuers announce share buybacks amid market volatility
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: Indonesian issuers announce buybacks of up to Rp1 trillion each at BREN, BRPT and TPIA
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The four Barito Group programs, including CUAN’s allocation reported as Rp300 billion in one account and up to Rp500 billion in another, total a reported Rp3.5 trillion. BREN and BRPT plan to run through 31 December, while TPIA’s reported end dates differ between 31 December and 19 January. Analysts said buybacks may absorb selling pressure but do not guarantee a recovery.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Telkom prepares to accelerate its Rp4 trillion share buyback
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: TLKM prepares to accelerate buyback of up to Rp4 trillion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: More than Rp3 trillion of the approved allocation remained on 19 October. Purchases are funded from internal cash and will be timed around market conditions and the company’s cash and investment needs, with the shareholder-approved program running through 8 June 2027.

market_structure_policy.event: IDX changes temporary auto-rejection-bottom limits to contain market panic
market_structure_policy.headline: IDX cuts temporary lower price limit to 7% on three boards
market_structure_policy.blurb: Effective 20 October through 31 December, the rule covers Main, Development and New Economy Board securities. Acceleration and Special Monitoring Board securities retain existing limits, and IDX said it would evaluate the measure based on market conditions.

market_structure_policy.event: OJK imposes Rp2.1 trillion in sanctions on DSSA, BREN and CUAN
market_structure_policy.headline: OJK imposes Rp2.1 trillion in sanctions on DSSA, BREN and CUAN
market_structure_policy.blurb: OJK set penalties at Rp1.5 trillion for Dian Swastatika Sentosa, Rp500 billion for Barito Renewables and Rp100 billion tied to Petrindo Jaya Kreasi, citing DSSA trading and BREN and CUAN IPOs. Petrindo said its penalty was not imposed directly on the company, while DSSA said its sanction would not materially affect its finances or operations.

earnings_guidance.event: DMAS reports nine-month presales against its revised 2026 target
earnings_guidance.headline: DMAS records Rp2.61 trillion in nine-month presales, 88.57% of revised target
earnings_guidance.blurb: Puradelta Lestari raised its 2026 target to Rp2.95 trillion, around 42% above the original goal, with industrial land sales mainly driven by data-center demand. Kiwoom Sekuritas and Mirae Asset Sekuritas view the revision as positive through 2027, while citing transaction realization, revenue and profit conversion, land availability and investment delays as risks.

earnings_guidance.event: Surya Semesta Internusa reports a return to profit in H1 2026
earnings_guidance.headline: SSIA returns to profit with Rp262.6 billion H1 2026 net profit
earnings_guidance.blurb: Surya Semesta's revenue rose 58.4% in H1, while marketing sales reached 24.1 hectares against a 135-hectare full-year target. Management targets Rp7.2 trillion in 2026 revenue and around Rp400 billion in net profit, with land sales realization remaining a challenge.

earnings_guidance.event: Bank Mandiri reports August asset and profit growth
earnings_guidance.headline: BMRI reports 20.7% asset and 22.3% net profit growth in August
earnings_guidance.blurb: Bank Mandiri reported bank-only assets of Rp2,359 trillion and net profit of Rp37.5 trillion. Loans and third-party funds each rose 17.6% year on year, to Rp1,592 trillion and Rp1,687 trillion, respectively. Finance & Strategy Director Novita Widya Anggraini said funding was supported by Livin' by Mandiri and Kopra by Mandiri.

earnings_guidance.event: BSI records Rp139 trillion in remittance transactions through September
earnings_guidance.headline: BRIS records Rp139 trillion in remittance transactions through September
earnings_guidance.blurb: Bank Syariah Indonesia said integration with its e-channels helped increase remittance-service users by 15%, supported by 15 remittance partners and 29 global partners. Corporate Secretary Wisnu Sunandar said the bank expects remittance growth this year to exceed last year's.

deals_control.event: WIFI controlling shareholder transfers a 26.667% stake to Sinergi Graha Kapital
deals_control.headline: WIFI controller transfers 26.667% stake to Sinergi Graha Kapital
deals_control.blurb: Solusi Sinergi Digital said Investasi Sukses Bersama sold 1.42 billion shares to SGK at Rp2,870 each for Rp4.06 trillion, for SGK’s long-term investment. ISB retained 27.756% and control, while SGK became a 26.667% shareholder. WIFI’s 21 October extraordinary meeting is set to decide on two executives’ resignations.

deals_control.event: Paradiso Resources increases its stake in NSSS to 5.85%
deals_control.headline: Paradiso Resources raises NSSS stake to 5.85%
deals_control.blurb: Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera said Paradiso acquired 414.63 million shares at Rp820 apiece on 15 October, paying Rp339.99 billion for direct investment. Its prior holding was 4.11%, and NSSS shares fell 6.31% to Rp520 on 20 October.

macro_flows.event: Rupiah weakens below Rp18,000 as authorities defend the currency
macro_flows.headline: Rupiah breaks through Rp18,000 as BI intervenes to defend currency
macro_flows.blurb: After falling through Rp18,000, the rupiah recovered 0.28% to Rp17,992 per US dollar on 20 October. President Prabowo ordered Bank Indonesia to defend the currency, and BI intervened in spot, swap, NDF and DNDF markets and bought government securities. Its rate decision is due 21 October.

macro_flows.event: Goldman Sachs estimates MSCI reclassification could trigger Indonesian fund outflows
macro_flows.headline: Goldman Sachs estimates MSCI reclassification could trigger US$5.6 billion in outflows
macro_flows.blurb: MSCI opened a consultation on 16 October on moving Indonesia from emerging-market to standalone status, citing insufficient progress on ownership transparency and trading conduct. Goldman Sachs says actively managed funds benchmarked to MSCI indexes hold more than US$8 billion in Indonesian stocks, with any sales dependent on managers’ strategies.

macro_flows.event: Mirae Asset estimates MSCI reclassification risks Indonesian bond outflows
macro_flows.headline: Mirae Asset estimates MSCI proposal could trigger US$3 billion in Indonesian bond outflows
macro_flows.blurb: Mirae Asset fixed-income analyst Jessica Tasijawa said the proposed shift from Emerging Market to Standalone Market could drive passive outflows of around US$3 billion before the final decision in June 2027. Since the 16 October announcement, foreign investors have sold Rp1.5 trillion of government bonds, and the 10-year yield has risen 11 bps to 7.36%.
